messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Re: Stan and RStan
parts:
Ummm, it’s complicated. I’m cc-ing Stan-dev because they’re the experts. Short story is: if you follow the instructions on the Rstan install page, it’ll also install the latest Stan.
A

> On Feb 12, 2015, at 8:31 PM, Phillip Price <pnp...@lbl.gov> wrote:
>
> The Stan website says RStan is the "R interface to Stan". Does this mean that if I download and install the most recent version of RStan, I am only getting the most recent interface, not the most recent version of Stan? From the plain language that I have installed the R interface to Stan, I would think the answer is Yes. But from the fact that I had to specify the number of cores I wanted to devote to it, I would think the answer is No, I have not just the most recent version of the interface but also the most recent version of Stan.
>
> I think it's the latter: I think when you say RStan is the "R interface to Stan" that you mean "RStan is a flavor of Stan that is accessed through R" or something like that. I think so, but I'm not sure.
>
> So: I just installed the most recent version of RStan. Am I up to date on all things Stannish?
>
> Remember, there are no stupid questions, only stupid questioners.
>
> Phil
>
>

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: Stan and RStan
parts:
English is my second language.  So regardless of what rstan means or implies, the answer to the last question is yes.  As a develop unit, RStan only provides interface to Stan.  But the released package rstan includes the source of Stan for now.  

In the future, the Stan source might be another R package (StanHeaders) that rstan depends/requires.  And installing a new version of rstan should require the installation of the most recent packaged Stan source.  So then the answer to the last question will still be yes. 

Jiqiang
